sources.entry: xsrv - Install and manage self-hosted services/applications, on your own server(s). (Source Code) GPL-3.0 Ansible/Shell

summary.one_liner: xsrv is a set of Ansible roles and an optional command-line tool for installing, configuring and maintaining self-hosted network services and applications on your own server(s).
summary.what_it_does: The project provides Ansible roles for automated installation and configuration of a range of services, including web serving (apache), DNS (dnsmasq), git forge (gitea), media (jellyfin), video conferencing (jitsi), file sharing (samba, nextcloud), chat (matrix), VPN (wireguard), and monitoring tools (grafana, victoriametrics, rsyslog, goaccess). It also includes an optional command-line tool for common operations, configuration, deployment and maintenance of servers. A template is provided to start with a single server in a few minutes. The README lists about 35 roles, with a common role described as base setup for Debian-based servers. Documentation covers installation, server and controller preparation, usage, configuration variables and tags.
use_cases: deploy a self-hosted git forge on my own server
set up Nextcloud file sync and sharing
automate installation of web services with Ansible
run a private Matrix chat or Jitsi video server
set up monitoring with Grafana and VictoriaMetrics
how_to_run: Read the Installation and Server preparation sections of the documentation
Create a first project from the provided template (First project)
Choose roles and set configuration variables as described in the configuration variable list
Run the Ansible playbooks to deploy the selected services to your server(s)
notable: Large collection of Ansible roles covering web, mail, chat, media, file storage, monitoring and AI services
Optional command-line tool for routine server operations, deployment and maintenance
Starter template for a single-server project
Includes helper roles for other ansible-based projects (readme_gen, nmap)
caveats: README does not state platform limits beyond referring to Debian-based servers for the common role
Setup requires familiarity with Ansible and a controller plus target server(s)
Full installation and configuration details live in the external documentation, not the README
keywords: deploy services on my own server
